chunks: 1750 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said regarding a man who gives dirhams to another to distribute, he said:

He will receive from the reward the like of what accrues to the giver, and nothing will be diminished from his reward. Even if the act of kindness were to pass through seventy hands, all of them would be rewarded without anything being diminished from the reward of its owner.

key_terms.الْأَجْرِ: reward from Allah for a righteous act
key_terms.الْمَعْرُوفَ: an act of goodness or kindness
key_terms.الْمُعْطِي: the one who gives the charity
key_terms.سَبْعِينَ: seventy, used here to indicate multiplicity
key_terms.صَاحِبِهِ: its original owner, meaning the primary giver

ai.seo_question: Does a person who distributes charity on behalf of someone else receive the same reward?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that anyone who assists in conveying charity shares in its reward. It emphasizes the expansive mercy of Allah, such that multiple people may be rewarded for facilitating good without any decrease in the reward of the original giver.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1750 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said regarding a man who distributes dirhams on behalf of another:

"He will receive a reward equal to that of the giver, without diminishing the giver's reward in any way. Even if the act of kindness passes through seventy hands, all of them will be rewarded without any reduction in the original giver's reward."
